messages:
maya: Heads-up — there's a new community model 'nebula-8' popping up in model-zoo. Can we do a quick intake for licensing + export checks? :eyes:
alejandro: link: https://repo.example.com/nebula-8 (model card + weights). license field says 'NC-Research-v1' — non-commercial research only.
sanjay: NC license usually blocks hosted API and commercial embeddings, right? Need legal on whether Dedicated or Private is OK if customer signs SLA.
jen: Also ran a tiny quant trial on a sample shard — using bitsandbytes 4-bit recipe. Quick command: `python quantize.py --model nebula-8 --bits 4 --backend bnb`
jen: got ~1.8x throughput improvement but small drop on copybench (EM down ~2%).
thomas: can you paste the exact license text? Some NC licenses differ a lot in derivative/work clauses.
alejandro: pasted snippet from model card: "Use permitted for non-commercial research; redistribution of fine-tuned checkpoints prohibited; commercial deployment prohibited."
model-gate-bot: Automated check: Detected export-control flags = none. Model provenance: trained on mixed-CC + curated crawls. Recommend manual review for personal data exposure.
legal-review: Quick read: NC clause prevents us from offering it via hosted API or charging for it. Dedicated customers could run it on their own infra if they accept the license terms — but we need to confirm redistribution prohibition: we cannot redistribute modified weights or host forked artifacts.
maya: So immediate gating: hosted = NO, Dedicated = possible if customer signs an acknowledgement, Private (VPC/on-prem) = OK?
legal-review: Private (customer-managed) is lower risk; still recommend we add a compliance checkbox to intake form: "no redistribution; confirm no commercial use" and require customer to accept.
sanjay: What about quantization artifacts? If we produce quantized versions for better perf, would that be considered redistribution/derivative?
legal-review: Likely yes — quantized weights are derived artifacts. We should not publish quantized checkpoints or ship them to customers if license forbids derivatives. Internal performance experiments for qualification are fine under research exception, but shipping artifacts to customers requires a license exception.
alejandro: Ok — treat quantized builds as internal-only. We'll document the results (metrics) but not upload artifacts.
jen: For evals, I ran standard eval set (llama-bench subset). Baseline perplexity 12.8, quant4 ppls ~13.5. Safety evals flagged hallucination on product names in 3% of probes.
maya: Prioritization question — do we invest infra time to certify nebula-8 for Dedicated? How many customers asked? Sales said 2 inbound interested for specialized academic labs (non-commercial).
thomas: If customers are non-commercial academic, they might be fine. But our dedicated product is billed — that looks like commercial activity. Need legal sign-off and explicit customer contract language.
legal-review: Suggest path: 1) Mark as "research-only" on model-catalog. 2) Disallow hosted. 3) Allow Private and on-prem. 4) Dedicated = possible only with legal-reviewed contract that states customers will not commercialize and that we will not redistribute quantized/modified weights.
maya: Action items: alejandro to update model-catalog entry with license flags + export notes; jen/sanjay to add quant experiment notes to internal runbook (no artifacts); legal-review to draft contract clause for Dedicated exceptions.
alejandro: Will update model-catalog now. Tagging internal flag: `license:NC-Research-v1`, `derivative_prohibited:true`, `hosted_allowed:false`.
jen: I'll drop eval logs into /internal/ml/bench/nebula-8/ (results only). Command used: `run_eval --model nebula-8 --suite llm_baseline --quant 4`
sanjay: Quick question — do we want to try a calibration pass (adapter-only fine-tune) to see if we can offer a hosted-compatible adapter instead of full weights? That might avoid redistributing base weights.
legal-review: Adapter-only might still be derivative depending on license wording. If adapter requires base weights to reproduce, distributing adapter could still indirectly enable commercial use. Need to include explicit language in contracts/terms.
thomas: For now, mark as "hold for hosted" and add a note: "Adapters require legal ok before distribution."
maya: Thanks everyone. I'll create a short ticket backlog: (1) model-catalog update, (2) runbook entries, (3) contract draft, (4) final go/no-go decision meeting next Tue. :+1:
model-gate-bot: Ticket created: ML-4782 (nebula-8 licensing intake)
alejandro: FYI — maintained mirror may appear in 3rd-party forks; watch for replication. I'll set a watcher on the repo.
jen: One last note — accuracy regressions after quant are small but measurable. If we can't ship quant artifacts, hosting cost for customers wanting better perf will be higher. Mention in contract SLA tradeoffs.
maya: Good point. We'll document cost/perf tradeoffs in the intake ticket. Closing for now.
